spots.name: Mercedes-Benz Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Mercedes-Benz Museum is an automobile museum in Stuttgart, Germany. It covers the history of the Mercedes-Benz brand and the brands associated with it. Stuttgart is home to the Mercedes-Benz brand and the international headquarters of the Mercedes-Benz Group.

spots.name: Bad Cannstatt
spots.summary: Bad Cannstatt, also called Cannstatt or Kannstadt, is one of the outer Stadtbezirke, or city boroughs, of Stuttgart in Baden-Württemberg, Germany. Bad Cannstatt is the oldest and most populous of Stuttgart's boroughs, and one of the most historically significant towns in the area of Stuttgart.

spots.name: Fernsehturm Stuttgart
spots.summary: Fernsehturm Stuttgart is a 216.61 m (710.7 ft) telecommunications tower in Stuttgart, Germany.

spots.name: Weissenhof Estate

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: The Weissenhof Estate is a housing estate built for the 1927 Deutscher Werkbund exhibition in Stuttgart, Germany. It was an international showcase of modern architecture's aspiration to provide inexpensive, simple, efficient, and good-quality housing.

spots.name: Old Castle

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Old Palace is a former castle located on the Schillerplatz in Stuttgart, Germany. The castle, originally a water castle dating back to the 10th century, was the residence of the Counts and later some Dukes of Württemberg and today is the home of the Landesmuseum Württemberg.

spots.name: Porsche Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Porsche Museum is an automobile museum in the Zuffenhausen district of Stuttgart, Germany on the site of carmaker Porsche. It ranks second among the most visited museums in Stuttgart, behind the Mercedes-Benz Museum. In 2015, it attracted approximately 450,000 visitors.

spots.name: Schlossplatz
spots.summary: Schlossplatz is the largest square in Stuttgart Mitte and home to the Neues Schloss which was built between 1746 and 1807. From its construction until the mid-1800s it was used as a military parade ground and not open to general public use.

spots.name: Stiftskirche, Stuttgart

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Stiftskirche is an inner-city church in Stuttgart, the capital of Baden-Württemberg, Germany. It is the main church of the Evangelical-Lutheran Church in Württemberg as well as the parish church of the evangelical (Lutheran) inner-city church district of Stuttgart.

spots.name: Solitude Palace
spots.summary: Solitude Palace is a Rococo schloss and hunting retreat commissioned by Charles Eugene, Duke of Württemberg. It was designed by Johann Friedrich Weyhing and Philippe de La Guêpière, and constructed from 1764 to 1769.

spots.name: Staatsgalerie Stuttgart

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Staatsgalerie Stuttgart is an art museum in Stuttgart, Germany, it opened in 1843. In 1984, the opening of the Neue Staatsgalerie designed by James Stirling transformed the once provincial gallery into one of Europe's leading museums.

spots.name: Wilhelma
spots.summary: Wilhelma is a zoological-botanical garden in Stuttgart, southern Germany, located in the Bad Cannstatt district in the north of the city on the grounds of a historic castle. Wilhelma Zoo is one of the most popular tourist destinations in Baden-Württemberg, seeing more than 2 million visitors annually.

spots.name: Stuttgart-Center
spots.summary: Stuttgart-Center is one of the five inner boroughs of the Germany city of Stuttgart. It is located at the very center, between Stuttgart-North, West, East and South, of the city on the banks of the Neckar about an hour from the Black Forest.

spots.name: Tagblatt-Turm
spots.summary: Tagblatt-Turm is a 61 m (200 ft), the 16-storey high-rise building in Stuttgart, Baden-Württemberg, Germany.

spots.name: Hegel House

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Museum Hegel House is a museum in Stuttgart, Germany.

spots.name: Württemberg Mausoleum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue

spots.summary: The Württemberg Mausoleum is a mausoleum located on the Württemberg, in the Rotenberg borough of Untertürkheim, in Stuttgart. It was designed by Giovanni Salucci for King William I of Württemberg to house the remains his second wife, Catherine Pavlovna of Russia.

spots.name: Landesmuseum Württemberg

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Landesmuseum Württemberg is the main historical museum of the Württemberg part of the German state of Baden-Württemberg. It emerged from the 16th-century “Kunstkammer” of the dukes, later kings, of Württemberg who resided in Stuttgart. As a museum it was founded in 1862 by King William I.

spots.name: Kunstmuseum Stuttgart

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Kunstmuseum Stuttgart is a contemporary and modern art museum in Stuttgart, Germany, built and opened in 2005.

spots.name: Neue Staatsgalerie

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Neue Staatsgalerie in Stuttgart, Germany, was designed by the British firm James Stirling, Michael Wilford and Associates, although largely accredited solely to partner James Stirling. It was constructed between 1979 and 1984. The building has been claimed as the epitome of Post-modernism.

spots.name: Stuttgart Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Stuttgart Cathedral or St Eberhard's Cathedral is a church in the German city of Stuttgart. It is dedicated to Saint Eberhard of Salzburg.

spots.name: Schillerplatz
spots.summary: Schillerplatz is a square in the old city centre of Stuttgart, Germany named in honour of the German poet, philosopher, historian, and dramatist Friedrich Schiller. Schillerplatz stands to the south west of Stuttgart's main square, Schlossplatz.

spots.name: Birkenkopf
spots.summary: The Birkenkopf is a prominent hill in Stuttgart, Germany. At an elevation of 511m, is almost 260m higher than city centre. It is in part a Schuttberg, an artificial hill built from the ruins and rubble from World War II.

spots.name: Wilhelm Palais

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Wilhelmspalais is a Palace located on the Charlottenplatz in Stuttgart-Mitte. It was the living quarters of the last Württemberg King, Wilhelm II. It was destroyed during World War II and between 1961 and 1965 reconstructed in modern style.

spots.name: Johanneskirche

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Protestant Church of St John in Stuttgart was built in the Gothic Revival style from 1864 to 1876 by its chief architect, Christian Friedrich von Leins. It lies on a peninsula of the Feuersee, while the main entrance and tower marks the beginning of the former Johannesstraße.

spots.name: Wirtemberg Castle

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wirtemberg Castle, a ruined hilltop castle, is the second family seat of the House of Württemberg, whose ancestors had abandoned Beutelsbach Castle.

spots.name: Rosenstein Palace
spots.summary: Rosenstein Castle is a palace in Stuttgart, Germany. It was designed in the classical style by the architect and court builder Giovanni Salucci (1769–1845) as the summer palace for King Wilhelm I of Württemberg, and was built between 1822 and 1830.

spots.name: House of History Baden-Württemberg

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The House of History Baden-Württemberg is a museum funded by the state of Baden-Württemberg in Stuttgart. It is located along the "Stuttgart Cultural Mile" on Konrad-Adenauer-Straße between the Staatsgalerie and the Musikhochschule.

spots.name: Killesbergpark
spots.summary: The Killesbergpark is an urban public park of half a square kilometre in Stuttgart, Germany. It is just north of the state capital, where Killesberg is a quarter of the borough of Stuttgart-Nord (North).

spots.name: Württemberg
spots.summary: The Württemberg is a hill on the territory of the German city of Stuttgart, capital of Baden-Württemberg.

spots.name: Linden Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Linden Museum is an ethnological museum located in Stuttgart, Germany. The museum features cultural artifacts from around the world, including South and Southeast Asia, Africa, the Islamic world from the Near East to Pakistan, China and Japan, as well as artifacts from North and Latin America and Oceania.

spots.name: Stadtbibliothek Stuttgart

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Stadtbibliothek Stuttgart is the public library of the city of Stuttgart. It is organized as a department of the city's cultural office and comprises the central library, 17 city district libraries, and two bookmobiles. In 2013, it received the national award as Library of the Year.

spots.name: Bismarck Tower (Stuttgart)
spots.summary: A small tower (20 m) northwest of the city centre, not far from Killesberg Tower.

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.name: MHPArena
spots.summary: MHPArena, formerly Neckarstadion, is a stadium located in Stuttgart, Baden-Württemberg, Germany, and home to Bundesliga club VfB Stuttgart. It hosted football matches in the 1974 FIFA World Cup, the UEFA Euro 1988, the 2006 FIFA World Cup, and the UEFA Euro 2024.

spots.name: Karlshöhe
spots.summary: A hill that separates the western and southern city. Walk uphill 10 minutes southern from S-Bahn-Station "Feuersee" through a park (via Senefelder Str, right to Reinsburgstr, left to Jean-Améry-Weg). Have an outlook and enjoy the beer garden.

spots.name: State Library of Württemberg

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The State Library of Württemberg is a large library in Stuttgart, Germany, which traces its history back to the ducal public library of Württemberg founded in 1765. It holds about 4 million volumes and is the fourth-largest library in the state of Baden-Württemberg.

spots.name: City Library at the Mailänder Platz

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Stuttgart's city library moved into this spectacular new building in 2011. It took 13 years of planning, an international architectural competition (which was won by Eun Young Yi from South Korea) and €80 million to complete it. spots.name: Stadtmuseum Stuttgart

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Stadtmuseum Stuttgart is a museum about the history of Stuttgart. It was opened in April of 2018 in the Wilhelm Palais, the former residence of Württembergs last King William II. The Stadtbibliothek Stuttgart, the public library of the city of Stuttgart, was also housed there from 1965 until 2011.

spots.name: Killesberg Tower
spots.summary: The Killesberg Tower is a 40-meter high observation tower located in the Killesberg Park in Stuttgart, Germany. Originally planned for the 1993 World Horticultural Exposition, an interruption in the design process delayed its erection until 8 years later in 2001.

spots.name: Weißenburgpark
spots.summary: A hill opposite to the Karlshöhe. Easy approach: it is a short hop from Station "Bopser" (U5, U6, U7). Outlook and nice Jugendstil-restaurant and beer garden (closes at 23:00)

spots.name: House of Music

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The House of Music is a music museum operated by the Landesmuseum Württemberg. It is housed in the Fruchtkasten, located on the Schillerplatz in downtown Stuttgart.

spots.name: Hohenheim Gardens
spots.summary: With an area of more than 30 hectares, the Hohenheim Gardens are the largest part of the campus of the University of Hohenheim in Stuttgart, Baden-Württemberg, Germany.

spots.name: Porsche-Arena
spots.summary: Porsche-Arena is a multi-purpose arena, located in Stuttgart, Germany. The seating capacity of the arena ranges from 5,100 to 8,000 people. It was opened in 2006, after 14 months of construction.

spots.name: Markthalle

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A beautiful Jugendstil market hall built in 1910.

spots.name: Königsbau
spots.summary: The Königsbau was erected 1856-1860 directly in front of the Neues Schloss as a multi-functional building to host commerce and special events, at the order of King Wilhem I (hence the name, which means "king's building"). Its Schlossplatz facade, with 34 columns over 135 metres, serves as a balance to the equally imposing palace opposite. In the latter half of the 20th century, the rebuilt Königsb

spots.name: Hauptbahnhof

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Railway Station was built in 1920 as a terminus station. The 56-meter-high tower with its rotating and illuminated Mercedes-Benz is one of the most famous city landmarks. On top of the tower there is an exhibition of the most controversial infrastructure project in Germany called S21. spots.name: Museum Hotel Silber

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Exhibition about the German secret police during World War II.

spots.name: Neues Schloss
spots.summary: The arguably most recognizable symbol of Stuttgart was constructed between 1746 and 1807 when the Duke of Württemberg, Carl Eugen, found the Altes Schloss and the erstwhile ducal residence in Ludwigsburg to be insufficiently stately. spots.name: Bohnenviertel
spots.summary: The Bohnenviertel is the only preserved part of Stuttgart's old town, having miraculously survived to the present day largely intact. Built mainly in the 14th century, it used to house the poorer part of the population, who fed mainly on beans which were grown all around the quarter in gardens and even hanging from the houses' walls, hence the name meaning "bean quarter". Today, the Bohnenviertel

spots.name: Sculpture Park
spots.summary: A small park showcasing sculptures from quasi-local artist Otto Hajek that spent big parts of his life in Stuttgart. At the end of the park is the ruin of the Hasenberg tower that was intentionally destroyed by the Germans in WW2.

spots.name: Calwer passage

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Small gallery with little stores (somewhat similar to Milan's famous gallery but a lot smaller). Right next to it is a building whose exterior is covered with plants.

spots.name: Schellenturm
spots.summary: One of the few remains of the city wall from the mid-16th century.
